questions.stem: The UNION BUDGET is presented every year on:

options.option_text: 1 FEBRUARY — advanced from last-day-of-Feb convention since 2017; Rail budget merged with Union Budget from 2017

questions.explanation: UNION BUDGET of INDIA ('Annual Financial Statement' per Art 112 of Constitution) — presented by FINANCE MINISTER in LOK SABHA annually. DATE: 1 FEBRUARY (since 2017; before that, last working day of February as inherited from British colonial practice). REASONS FOR SHIFT: (a) earlier presentation → earlier passage → implementation from 1 April; (b) benefits agri + state budgets. RAIL BUDGET — separately presented since 1924 (Acworth Committee); MERGED with Union Budget from 2017 (first merged = Arun Jaitley 2017 budget). CALENDAR: (1) 1 FEB — FM presents budget speech ~2 hours; tabled documents. (2) 2 Feb – next ~10 days — general discussion in both Houses. (3) Feb-Mar (1-month recess) — STANDING COMMITTEES scrutinise DEMANDS FOR GRANTS ministry-wise. (4) 2nd half of March – early April — voting on Demands + passage of APPROPRIATION BILL + FINANCE BILL. (5) FINANCIAL YEAR starts 1 APRIL. BUDGET DOCUMENTS (14+ key ones): (1) Annual Financial Statement (Art 112 — main document). (2) Demands for Grants. (3) Finance Bill (Art 110). (4) Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement (FRBM Act). (5) Medium Term Fiscal Policy Statement. (6) Macroeconomic Framework Statement. (7) Expenditure Budget Vol-I/II. (8) Receipts Budget. (9) Budget at a Glance. (10) Memorandum explaining tax proposals. (11) Output Outcome Framework. (12) Key Features of Budget. Also ECONOMIC SURVEY presented DAY BEFORE Budget (31 Jan) by Chief Economic Adviser — reviews previous year + projections. BUDGET structure: (1) REVENUE BUDGET = Revenue Receipts (taxes + non-tax) + Revenue Expenditure (salaries, interest, subsidies, pensions — recurring, doesn't create assets). (2) CAPITAL BUDGET = Capital Receipts (borrowings, disinvestment) + Capital Expenditure (infrastructure, loans — creates assets). FUNDS: (1) CONSOLIDATED FUND OF INDIA (CFI) — Art 266(1); all govt revenues + loans; need Parliament authorisation to spend. (2) PUBLIC ACCOUNT — Art 266(2); provident funds, small savings etc.; govt as banker. (3) CONTINGENCY FUND — Art 267; ₹30,000 cr corpus; at President's disposal for unforeseen expenses; must be subsequently approved by Parliament. FMS WHO PRESENTED BUDGETS: MORARJI DESAI (10 — record), P. Chidambaram (9), Pranab Mukherjee (8), Yashwant Sinha (8), Manmohan Singh (6), Arun Jaitley (5), Nirmala Sitharaman (7+, 2019-25, LONGEST CONSECUTIVELY serving FM for budgets).

questions.stem: The FRBM Act 2003 set targets for FISCAL CONSOLIDATION. It stipulates:

options.option_text: Fiscal deficit target of 3% of GDP (originally 2008-09, missed), revenue deficit target 0%; debt target 40% of GDP for Centre, 20% for states

questions.explanation: FRBM ACT (Fiscal Responsibility + Budget Management Act) 2003 — aimed at FISCAL DISCIPLINE + prudent debt management. ENACTED 2003, effective 5 July 2004. Operationalised the 2000 K.P. Geethakrishnan Committee + 2003 Kelkar Task Force. ORIGINAL TARGETS (to be met by 2008-09): (1) FISCAL DEFICIT ≤ 3% of GDP. (2) REVENUE DEFICIT = 0 (balanced revenue account — subsequently dropped; replaced with 'effective revenue deficit' concept). (3) Pre-decided reductions: FD 0.3%/yr, RD 0.5%/yr. (4) No RBI FINANCING (ad hoc treasury bills) of deficit post 2006. TARGETS MISSED: 2008-09 global financial crisis + counter-cyclical spending; 2020-21 COVID. FD was 3.4% in 2018-19; shot up to 9.2% in 2020-21 (COVID); now gradually declining. REVISED TARGETS (N.K. Singh Committee 2017 recommendations adopted in 2018 amendments): (a) FISCAL DEFICIT — 3% by 2020-21 (missed); (b) REVENUE DEFICIT — 2.1% by 2019-20 (missed); (c) GENERAL GOVERNMENT DEBT = 60% of GDP (40% Centre + 20% states) by 2024-25. CURRENT STATUS (FY 2024-25 Budget): FD = 4.9% (Centre); all-India (Centre + States) ~9-10%. GDP-to-debt ratio ~58% (Centre) + ~28% (states) = ~86% total (includes public sector enterprises too). BUDGET 2024-25 (Nirmala Sitharaman): (a) FD target 4.9% for FY25; 4.5% for FY26; (b) Capex push continues; (c) gross borrowings ₹14.01 lakh crore. KEY FISCAL CONCEPTS: (1) FISCAL DEFICIT (FD) = Total Expenditure – Total Revenue Receipts (exc. borrowings). Measures total govt borrowing need. (2) REVENUE DEFICIT (RD) = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts. Indicates dis-saving. (3) PRIMARY DEFICIT (PD) = FD - Interest payments. Indicates NEW borrowing (minus servicing old debt). (4) EFFECTIVE REVENUE DEFICIT (ERD) — introduced 2011; = RD - Grants for creation of capital assets. (5) GROSS FISCAL DEFICIT (GFD) vs NET (net of net lending). SOURCES OF FD FINANCING: (a) MARKET BORROWING (dated G-Secs via RBI auctions); (b) small savings (NSSF); (c) external borrowings (concessional — World Bank, ADB); (d) draw-down of cash balances. KEY ISSUE: CROWDING-OUT of private investment — govt borrowing increases interest rates + absorbs loanable funds. COUNTER-CYCLICAL fiscal policy OK during recessions (2008, 2020) but must consolidate during growth phases.

questions.stem: The GST (Goods + Services Tax) was rolled out in India on:

options.option_text: 1 JULY 2017 — 'One Nation, One Tax'; 101st Constitutional Amendment 2016; 4 slabs 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%; CGST + SGST + IGST + UTGST components

questions.explanation: GST (GOODS + SERVICES TAX) — INDIA's BIGGEST INDIRECT TAX REFORM since Independence. ROLLED OUT midnight 30 Jun / 1 JULY 2017 in Parliament's CENTRAL HALL by President Pranab Mukherjee + PM Modi. 'ONE NATION, ONE TAX, ONE MARKET'. 101ST CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT ACT 2016 created legal basis (Art 246A, 269A, 279A — GST Council). PATH: proposed 2000 (Atal Bihari Vajpayee), Empowered Committee (Asim Dasgupta), 115th CAB 2011 lapsed, 122nd CAB 2014 passed in 2016 as 101st CAA. STRUCTURE — 'DUAL GST': (1) CGST (Central GST) — central component; (2) SGST (State GST) — state component; (3) IGST (Integrated GST) — on inter-state supply + imports, collected by Centre, apportioned to destination state; (4) UTGST (Union Territory GST) — for UTs without legislature. PRINCIPLE: DESTINATION-based tax (where consumed, not produced — benefits consuming states). SLABS: (a) 0% — essential goods (fresh food, milk, educational services, healthcare, unbranded atta/dal/rice, sanitary pads since 2018, cereals, natural honey); (b) 5% — mass consumption (packaged food, tea, coffee, sugar, edible oil, medicines, transport); (c) 12% — processed food, butter, ghee, ayurvedic medicines, mobile phones (some); (d) 18% — most services + mid-range goods (toothpaste, hair oil, shoes >₹500, hotel 1000-7500); (e) 28% — luxury + demerit (cars, refrigerators, washing machines, tobacco, aerated drinks, cement); PLUS GST COMPENSATION CESS on tobacco + luxury cars + coal (max 15% cess; 200%+ on cigarettes). SPECIAL RATES: Gold 3%, Rough diamond 0.25%. ABSORBED ~17 indirect taxes: Central Excise Duty, Service Tax, Additional Customs Duty, VAT, Entry Tax, Octroi, Luxury Tax, Entertainment Tax, Purchase Tax, Central Sales Tax, State Surcharges, etc. NOT under GST: Alcohol (states' revenue), Petroleum (petrol, diesel, ATF, crude oil, natural gas — states' revenue), Electricity duty, Stamp duty. THRESHOLD: exempt for businesses with turnover <₹40 lakh (services ₹20 lakh in North-East). COMPOSITION SCHEME — ₹1.5 cr turnover. GST COUNCIL — constitutional body (Art 279A); chaired by Finance Minister; all state FMs + 2 Union Ministers; Centre has 1/3 vote weight, states 2/3 collectively; decisions by 3/4 majority. Meets periodically. GSTN (GST Network) — IT backbone for returns, invoicing, input tax credit. GST MONTHLY COLLECTIONS: crossed ₹1 lakh crore regularly since 2019, ₹2 lakh crore first in April 2024; FY24-25 estimated ₹22-24 lakh crore. GST COMPENSATION to states: Centre compensated for 5 years (2017-2022) for revenue shortfall below 14% growth (Compensation Cess fund). 5-year guarantee ended June 2022 + not extended. Some states (TN, Kerala, WB) demand further support.

questions.stem: India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth rate in FY 2023-24 was:

options.option_text: 8.2% (provisional estimate) — making India the FASTEST-growing major economy; real GDP growth consistently 6-8% over 2013-2025 except COVID dip

questions.explanation: INDIA's GDP GROWTH — fastest among major economies. RECENT FY FIGURES (real GDP growth): (a) FY 2019-20: 3.9% (pre-COVID slowdown); (b) FY 2020-21: -5.8% (COVID contraction); (c) FY 2021-22: 9.7% (rebound); (d) FY 2022-23: 7.0%; (e) FY 2023-24: 8.2% (second advance estimate; provisional 8.2%); (f) FY 2024-25: 6.5-7% (projection). Nominal GDP FY 2023-24: ₹295 LAKH CRORE (~$3.5 TRILLION). India = 5TH LARGEST ECONOMY by nominal GDP (overtook UK 2022); 3RD LARGEST by PPP (after China + USA). Projected to be 3rd largest nominal by 2028. BASIC GDP CONCEPTS: (1) GDP — total value of all goods + services produced WITHIN country's borders in a year. (2) GNP — GDP + net factor income from abroad (NFIA) = GDP + (income earned by Indians abroad) - (income earned by foreigners in India). For India, GNP typically SLIGHTLY LESS than GDP (more foreign investment in India than Indian investment abroad, generating net factor income outflow). (3) NDP / NNP — subtract DEPRECIATION. (4) NOMINAL vs REAL: (a) Nominal = current-year prices; (b) Real = base-year prices (measures true output growth, excludes inflation). India's base year 2011-12 (pending change to 2020-21). (5) MARKET PRICES vs FACTOR COST: Market price = Factor cost + Indirect taxes - Subsidies. 3 METHODS to calculate GDP: (1) PRODUCTION / VALUE ADDED — sum of GVA across sectors (agri + industry + services). (2) INCOME — wages + rent + interest + profits. (3) EXPENDITURE — C + I + G + (X - M). In INDIA, MAIN method is Production method; from Jan 2015, new series with GVA at basic prices central metric. SECTORAL CONTRIBUTION to GVA (FY24): AGRICULTURE 17% (but 46% workforce — low productivity), INDUSTRY 27% (Manufacturing 14% — LOW by Asian standards; Make in India aims 25%), SERVICES 56% (IT + finance + tourism + retail). INDIA UNIQUE — service-led growth bypassing manufacturing-intensive phase (contrast with China, Vietnam). PER CAPITA INCOME (FY24): ~$2,700 = ₹2.30 lakh/year. Still relatively LOW (WORLD avg $12,000; USA $80,000). India's GDP per capita PPP ~$10,000. CENTRAL STATISTICS OFFICE (CSO) / NSO — under Ministry of Statistics + Programme Implementation (MoSPI) — releases GDP data. National Accounts Statistics (NAS) annual publication. Quarterly GDP data released 2 months after quarter end. POVERTY: ~10% multidimensional poor (NITI Aayog MPI 2023, from 29% in 2013-14); 13.5 CRORE people lifted from MPI 2015-16 to 2019-21.

questions.stem: In a PROGRESSIVE income tax system (like India's), the tax RATE:

options.option_text: INCREASES as income rises — higher income → higher marginal tax rate; pro-redistribution; based on 'ability to pay' principle

questions.explanation: PROGRESSIVE TAX SYSTEM — tax rate INCREASES as taxable income rises. Principle: those with GREATER ABILITY TO PAY bear HIGHER proportional tax burden. Higher tax brackets on richer earners. INDIA's INCOME TAX system is PROGRESSIVE. TYPES of TAXATION: (1) PROGRESSIVE — most income tax (India, USA, UK, most countries); social equity favoured. (2) REGRESSIVE — rate DECREASES with higher income (e.g., sales tax + GST hurts poor more as share of income); demerit taxes (on tobacco, fuel) fall harder on poor proportionally. (3) PROPORTIONAL / FLAT — uniform rate regardless of income (e.g., 20% on everyone); simpler but less equitable. INDIA INCOME TAX REGIMES (AY 2024-25): NEW TAX REGIME (default from FY 2023-24, simplified, fewer deductions): (a) ₹0-3 LAKH: NIL; (b) ₹3-7 LAKH: 5%; (c) ₹7-10 LAKH: 10%; (d) ₹10-12 LAKH: 15%; (e) ₹12-15 LAKH: 20%; (f) >₹15 LAKH: 30%. STANDARD DEDUCTION: ₹75,000. Total REBATE u/s 87A: up to ₹25,000 (so effective NIL tax up to ₹7 LAKH income). PLUS 4% Health + Education Cess. SURCHARGE on HNI: 10% (>₹50L), 15% (>₹1 Cr), 25% (>₹2 Cr), 37% (>₹5 Cr) — max marginal rate ~42.7% under old regime; REDUCED to 25% maximum surcharge under new regime (max marginal ~39%). OLD TAX REGIME (optional; more deductions — 80C ₹1.5 L, 80D medical, HRA, LTA, home loan interest ₹2L u/s 24b, NPS 80CCD, etc.): (a) ₹0-2.5 L NIL; (b) ₹2.5-5 L 5%; (c) ₹5-10 L 20%; (d) >₹10 L 30%. TAX on INDIVIDUALS + HUFs + firms + corporates. CORPORATE TAX: (a) Domestic companies — 22% (new regime, no deductions) + 4% cess = ~25% effective; 25% (regime 1 with deductions); 15% for new manufacturing companies. (b) Foreign companies — 40% + surcharge + cess. TYPES OF TAXES IN INDIA: (1) DIRECT (Individual / Corp / Wealth / Gift / Securities Transaction Tax) — paid directly; progressive; IMPOSED by CENTRE (incl income tax), administered by CBDT (Central Board of Direct Taxes). (2) INDIRECT (GST, Customs, Excise on alcohol/petroleum, Stamp Duty) — consumer ultimately pays via price; often regressive. CBIC (CBEC renamed 2018) = Central Board of Indirect Taxes + Customs. DIRECT TAX CODE (DTC) — proposed comprehensive overhaul; pending. TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) + TCS (Tax Collected at Source) — collection mechanisms. ITR (Income Tax Return) FILING due 31 July (individuals), 31 Oct (companies). STATS: ~7.5 CRORE ITRs filed FY24; tax-to-GDP ratio ~12% (low; OECD avg 34%). DIRECT tax share has been growing; ~55% of Central tax revenue now direct.

questions.stem: The 15th FINANCE COMMISSION (Chair: N.K. Singh) recommended the SHARE of NET CENTRAL TAXES devolved to STATES (2020-2026) at:

options.option_text: 41% (down from 14th FC's 42%, to accommodate J&K UT out of state pool); states' collective share of divisible pool

questions.explanation: FINANCE COMMISSION (FC) — constitutional body under Article 280, constituted by PRESIDENT every 5 years (or earlier); recommends DEVOLUTION of resources + transfers between Centre + States. COMPOSITION: 1 Chairman + 4 members (qualifications specified). FUNCTIONS: (1) Distribution of NET PROCEEDS of taxes between Centre + States (vertical devolution). (2) Distribution among states (horizontal — based on formula). (3) Principles governing GRANTS-IN-AID to states (Art 275). (4) Measures to augment state consolidated funds for local bodies (panchayats + municipalities) since 73rd + 74th CAAs. (5) Any other matter in interests of sound finance. FCs SO FAR: (1) 1st FC (K.C. Neogy, 1952): states got 10%. (2) 10th FC (KC Pant, 1995-2000): started sharing all taxes (80th CAA 2000 after recommendations). (3) 13th FC (Vijay Kelkar, 2010-15): 32% devolution. (4) 14th FC (Y.V. Reddy, 2015-2020): 42% devolution (BIGGEST JUMP — 10 percentage points); major shift towards state autonomy. (5) 15th FC (N.K. SINGH, 2020-21 + 2021-26): recommended 41% devolution for 2020-26 (reduced by 1% to accommodate J&K becoming a Union Territory, which reduced state pool). Also HORIZONTAL formula. (6) 16th FC (ARVIND PANAGARIYA, appointed Dec 2023) — constituted for 2026-31 period; will submit 2025. 15TH FC's HORIZONTAL DEVOLUTION FORMULA (among states): (a) INCOME DISTANCE 45% — per capita income gap from highest-income state (Haryana) — REWARDS POORER states (equity); (b) POPULATION (2011 census) 15% — used 2011 census (earlier FCs used 1971 census for population — controversial as South with good family planning felt penalised; FC-15 switched to 2011 — controversial for South too); (c) AREA 15%; (d) FOREST + ECOLOGY 10%; (e) DEMOGRAPHIC PERFORMANCE 12.5% (penalises high fertility); (f) TAX EFFORT 2.5%. TOP BENEFICIARIES (highest share): UP (17.94%), Bihar (10.06%), MP (7.85%), West Bengal (7.52%), Maharashtra (6.32%). LEAST: Goa (0.39%), Sikkim (0.39%), Mizoram (0.50%). CRITIQUE: SOUTH STATES (Kerala, Karnataka, TN, AP, Telangana) feel penalised despite better governance + fiscal discipline + lower fertility — lost share under 15th FC despite good record. Inter-State Council + NITI Aayog also forums for cooperative federalism. 15th FC also recommended: (1) revenue deficit grants to 17 states; (2) grants for health (₹1.06 lakh cr); (3) grants for local bodies (₹4.36 lakh cr for rural + urban); (4) performance-based incentives; (5) disaster management grants. 16TH FC under Panagariya is studying above issues + GST reform + GST Council integration + state-specific concerns + Southern states' demand.

questions.stem: INFLATION, measured by the CONSUMER PRICE INDEX (CPI), is BASED on:

options.option_text: A BASKET of goods + services consumed by typical household — India base 2012 with food 45.86% weight; RBI targets 4% ± 2%

questions.explanation: INFLATION — general, sustained rise in prices of goods + services in an economy; reduces purchasing power of money. Opposite: DEFLATION (falling prices). INFLATION INDICES in INDIA: (1) CPI (Consumer Price Index) — reflects RETAIL prices; most relevant for consumers. INDIA uses CPI-Combined (urban + rural, 2012 base), published by NSO (National Statistical Office). WEIGHTS: FOOD + BEVERAGES 45.86%, miscellaneous 28.32%, housing 10.07%, fuel + light 6.84%, clothing + footwear 6.53%, pan/tobacco 2.38%. Since 2016 — RBI has STATUTORY inflation target of 4% ± 2% (i.e., 2-6% band) — FLEXIBLE INFLATION TARGETING; failure to stay in band for 3 consecutive quarters requires report to Centre. (2) WPI (Wholesale Price Index) — wholesale prices of goods (no services); OFFICE of ECONOMIC ADVISER, DPIIT; 2011-12 base, 697 items. WEIGHTS: manufactured products 64.2%, primary articles 22.6%, fuel + power 13.15%. WPI tends to be more VOLATILE than CPI (dominated by commodity prices); used for indexation of govt payments. (3) CPI-IW (Industrial Workers) — labour ministry; used for DA (Dearness Allowance) calculation for central govt employees. (4) CPI-AL (Agricultural Labourers), CPI-RL (Rural Labourers). INFLATION TYPES: (1) DEMAND-PULL — 'too much money chasing too few goods'; aggregate demand > supply; e.g., consumer boom, govt spending boost. (2) COST-PUSH — rising input costs (oil, raw materials, wages) pushed to consumer prices; e.g., oil price shocks 1973, Russia-Ukraine 2022. (3) STRUCTURAL — long-run supply bottlenecks (agri rigidities, infrastructure). (4) IMPORTED inflation — rupee depreciation → costlier imports → inflation. (5) HEADLINE vs CORE: Headline = overall CPI; Core = CPI excluding volatile food + fuel. CAUSES + REMEDIES: (a) Monetary — RBI raises repo rate to tame inflation; (b) Fiscal — cut government spending, raise taxes; (c) Supply side — boost production, reduce bottlenecks; (d) Trade — reduce import duties on inflation-sensitive items. MODERATE inflation (4-6%) considered HEALTHY — signals growing economy, gives small margin for adjustment. HYPER-inflation (>50%/month) = Zimbabwe 2008, Weimar Germany 1923, Venezuela 2018-22, Yugoslavia 1994 — catastrophic. STAGFLATION — stagnation + inflation together (1970s US + UK, 2022 worries). DISINFLATION — slowing inflation rate (still positive). DEFLATION — negative inflation (Japan 1990s-2010s). INDIA's CPI inflation: 6.7% (FY22-23), 5.4% (FY23-24, provisional), 4.5% (FY24-25 projection) — on downward path. FOOD PRICES are VOLATILE + key driver (tomato + onion spikes of 2023). MSP + buffer stocks + PDS moderate food inflation.

questions.stem: The INDIAN FIVE-YEAR PLANS ended with the 12th Plan (2012-17). They have been replaced by:

options.option_text: NITI Aayog's 3-YEAR ACTION AGENDAS / 7-year strategy / 15-year vision document + annual budgets; Planning Commission scrapped Jan 2015

questions.explanation: INDIA'S PLANNING EVOLUTION: PLANNING COMMISSION (1950-2014) — set up by Nehru Cabinet resolution 15 March 1950; chaired by PM; produced 12 FIVE-YEAR PLANS. SCRAPPED 1 January 2015 by Modi govt; REPLACED by NITI AAYOG (National Institution for Transforming India). REASONS for SCRAPPING: (1) Outdated Soviet-style top-down planning; (2) weakening of states' autonomy; (3) inefficient bureaucracy; (4) poor coordination. NITI AAYOG — created by Cabinet resolution 1 Jan 2015. STRUCTURE: (1) Chairperson — PM; (2) VICE-CHAIRMAN (currently Suman K. Bery, 2022-); (3) CEO (B.V.R. Subrahmanyam, IAS, 2023-); (4) Governing Council = all state CMs + UT LGs + PM; (5) Regional Councils; (6) Full-time members + ex-officio members + special invitees. FUNCTIONS: (1) 'THINK-TANK' — research + policy analysis; (2) Cooperative + COMPETITIVE FEDERALISM; (3) facilitates states + Centre cooperation. NO allocatory power over centrally sponsored schemes (transferred to Finance Ministry). (4) Strategic + long-term direction. KEY DOCUMENTS by NITI Aayog: (1) '3-YEAR ACTION AGENDA' (2017-20). (2) '7-YEAR STRATEGY FOR NEW INDIA @ 75' — vision for 2022. (3) '15-YEAR VISION DOCUMENT' (long-term). (4) 'SDG INDIA INDEX' annual — state-wise performance on Sustainable Development Goals. (5) 'NATIONAL HEALTH INDEX' annual. (6) 'COMPOSITE WATER MANAGEMENT INDEX'. (7) 'ASPIRATIONAL DISTRICTS PROGRAMME' (115 districts, 2018; ~500+ blocks in 2023 expansion). (8) 'EXPORT PREPAREDNESS INDEX'. (9) 'ATAL INNOVATION MISSION' (Atal Tinkering Labs, incubators). (10) 'Multidimensional Poverty Index'. (11) 'AIM-Start-up India' linkage. PAST 5-YEAR PLANS (summary): (a) 1st (1951-56) — Mahalanobis-Harrod-Domar; agri + irrigation focus. Growth 3.6%. (b) 2nd (1956-61) — Mahalanobis model; heavy industry + PSUs (steel plants — Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur). Growth 4.1%. (c) 3rd (1961-66) — self-sustaining growth; failed due to Indo-China war, droughts. Growth 2.4%. Three ANNUAL PLANS (1966-69) 'plan holidays'. (d) 4th (1969-74) — Indira's 'Garibi Hatao'; Bank nationalisation; Green Revolution. Growth 3.3%. (e) 5th (1974-79) — Emergency era; truncated. (f) 6th (1980-85) — IRDP; MMGs. (g) 7th (1985-90) — productivity. (h) 8th (1992-97) — LPG reforms continued; Manmohan; growth 6.8%. (i) 9th (1997-2002) — infra. (j) 10th (2002-07) — Vajpayee; growth 7.8%. (k) 11th (2007-12) — UPA-II; growth 8.1%; inclusive. (l) 12TH PLAN (2012-17) — last. Growth 6.9% avg. Since 2015: ANNUAL BUDGETS + periodic strategy documents replace 5YP structure.

questions.stem: India's Foreign Exchange Reserves (FOREX), a major economic indicator, are maintained by:

options.option_text: RBI (Reserve Bank of India) — hold reserves to stabilise Rupee + meet imports + investor confidence; INDIA has 4TH LARGEST reserves globally (~$650-700 B)

questions.explanation: FOREX RESERVES (Foreign Exchange Reserves) — foreign currency holdings of central bank + government. INDIA's RBI manages them. CURRENT LEVEL (2024-25): ~$700 BILLION (record high; was $100 B in 2003, $300 B in 2015, $600 B in 2021). INDIA = 4TH LARGEST forex holder globally (after CHINA $3.3 T, JAPAN $1.3 T, SWITZERLAND ~$900 B; USA ~$250 B — low since USD is reserve currency). COMPONENTS of INDIA's forex reserves: (1) FOREIGN CURRENCY ASSETS (FCA) — ~$610 B; mostly USD (~60%), EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD. Held in US Treasury securities, AAA bonds, deposits with central banks + BIS. (2) GOLD — ~$60 B; 820+ TONNES (RBI holds 30%+ abroad — BoE Vaults London, BIS). (3) SDRs (Special Drawing Rights) — ~$18 B; IMF reserve asset, basket of 5 currencies. (4) RESERVE POSITION in IMF — ~$5 B. FORMULA: forex reserves should cover MINIMUM 3-6 MONTHS of imports (India's 2024 imports ~$720B → ~10 months of reserves = STRONG cushion). IMPORTANCE: (1) manage EXCHANGE RATE (RBI intervenes by buying/selling USD to prevent sharp rupee swings); (2) meet IMPORT needs (especially oil, gold); (3) SERVICE EXTERNAL DEBT; (4) investor CONFIDENCE signal; (5) meet contingencies (COVID, war, crisis); (6) prevent currency crises. HISTORIC CRISIS: 1991 BoP CRISIS — forex reserves fell to ~$1 BILLION (only 2 WEEKS of imports); India had to PLEDGE 47 TONNES OF GOLD to Bank of England + Union Bank of Switzerland in May-July 1991 to raise $400M for imports; PM Chandra Shekhar, FM Yashwant Sinha; triggered LPG REFORMS under Narasimha Rao + Manmohan Singh from July 1991. EXCHANGE RATE REGIMES: (1) FIXED — currency pegged to another (like Hong Kong Dollar to USD). (2) FLOATING — market-determined (US, UK, EU). (3) MANAGED FLOAT — India's system; market-determined but RBI intervenes to curb excess volatility. INR has been managed float since 1993. RUPEE HISTORY: 1947 — ₹1 = $1 (parity with USD); 1966 — ₹4.76/$ (devaluation); 1991 — ₹17.50 → 24.50 (devaluation); 2013 — ₹60; 2022-23 — ₹83; 2024 — ₹83-85. Rupee has depreciated ~35% since 2013 vs USD. CAPITAL ACCOUNT: India has PARTIAL capital account convertibility (Tarapore Committee 1997, 2006 roadmaps). Current account fully convertible since 1994 (LERMS abolished). FDI routes: automatic + government approval. FCRA (Foreign Contribution Regulation Act) for NGO forex receipts. FEMA 1999 replaced FERA 1973. BoP (Balance of Payments) = Current Account (trade + services + transfers) + Capital Account (FDI + FII + ECBs + banking). India typically runs CAD (Current Account Deficit) ~1-2% of GDP + capital surplus.

questions.stem: MUDRA scheme for small business financing was launched in 2015. What does MUDRA stand for?

options.option_text: Ministry of Urban Development + Rural Affairs

questions.explanation: MUDRA — MICRO UNITS DEVELOPMENT + REFINANCE AGENCY. PMMY (PRADHAN MANTRI MUDRA YOJANA) LAUNCHED 8 APRIL 2015 by PM Modi. OBJECTIVE: 'FUND the UNFUNDED' — provide LOANS up to ₹10 LAKH to NON-CORPORATE, NON-FARM SMALL/MICRO ENTERPRISES without COLLATERAL. LOAN CATEGORIES: (1) SHISHU — up to ₹50,000 (small starters — street vendors, kirana shops, tailors, beauty parlours); (2) KISHOR — ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh (established small businesses); (3) TARUN — ₹5 lakh to ₹10 LAKH (expanding businesses). (4) TARUN PLUS — ₹10-20 LAKH added in Budget 2024-25 for existing Tarun beneficiaries who repaid previous loans. LENDERS: scheduled COMMERCIAL BANKS, REGIONAL RURAL BANKS, SMALL FINANCE BANKS, MFIs (Microfinance Institutions), NBFCs, Cooperative Banks. MUDRA itself REFINANCES these lenders. OWNERSHIP: MUDRA is a subsidiary of SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India, est. 1990, HQ Lucknow). PROGRESS (as of 2024): ~45 CRORE PMMY loans disbursed; ₹26+ lakh crore sanctioned. ~67% to women beneficiaries. ~50% to SC/ST/OBC. ~75% loans <₹50,000 (Shishu segment). BROAD IMPACT on informal sector. ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES: Manufacturing, Trading, Service Sector, Agri (allied — dairy, poultry, fishery, bee-keeping). NOT for crop loans. INTEREST: varies by lender (not prescribed); typically 8-12% p.a. Collateral NOT required. Mudra Card = debit-card-like working-capital credit. OTHER SIMILAR SCHEMES: (1) STAND-UP INDIA (5 April 2016) — ₹10 lakh-1 CRORE loans for SC/ST + WOMEN entrepreneurs per bank branch. Over 2.5 lakh sanctioned. (2) STARTUP INDIA (16 Jan 2016) — 3-year tax exemption, IP fast-track, self-certification; 1.4+ lakh startups recognised by DPIIT; India's STARTUP ECOSYSTEM = 3rd largest globally (after USA + China) with 100+ UNICORNS (valued >$1B): Byju's, Flipkart, Paytm, Zomato, Swiggy, OYO, Ola, Nykaa, PhysicsWallah, etc. (3) PM SVANIDHI (2020) — ₹10,000 to ₹50,000 loans to STREET VENDORS (post-COVID support); 56 lakh+ loans. (4) PM VISHWAKARMA (17 Sep 2023) — support for traditional artisans (18 trades — carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters, boatmakers, etc.); training, toolkit grant, loans up to ₹3 lakh. (5) EMERGENCY CREDIT LINE GUARANTEE SCHEME (ECLGS, May 2020) — COVID collateral-free MSME loans; ₹5 lakh crore disbursed; credited with saving MSME sector. (6) CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro + Small Enterprises, 2000) — collateral-free credit up to ₹5 crore for MSMEs; guarantee cover 75-85%. FINANCIAL INCLUSION DRIVE: JAM trinity (Jan Dhan + Aadhaar + Mobile) + PMJDY + UPI + PMMY together transformed access to finance for unbanked.
